subject.title: Compaction dead-end: recently-compacted session with overflow blocks permanently

question: When a compaction attempt is safely classified as already compacted but the active session still cannot fit the next turn, should OpenClaw rotate to a new session, require an explicit in-product recovery action, or retain the existing fail-closed behavior while improving diagnosis?
rationale: Each option changes user-visible continuity, queued-message handling, and the preservation of potentially valuable session context; source-level control-flow changes cannot safely choose that policy alone.

options.title: Rotate while preserving history
options.body: After a proven no-progress condition, retain the old transcript read-only, start a new session, notify the user, and define how queued messages are resumed.

options.title: Offer explicit recovery
options.body: Keep the session blocked but provide an in-product reset or new-session action with a clear explanation and no silent state loss.

options.title: Keep fail-closed with diagnostics
options.body: Preserve the current safety behavior but add a precise blocked-session message and diagnostic path while gathering more live evidence.

recommendation.title: Rotate while preserving history
recommendation.body: After a proven no-progress condition, retain the old transcript read-only, start a new session, notify the user, and define how queued messages are resumed.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor is most closely connected in history to the existing mid-turn compaction recovery flow and the overlapping open proposal.
